blindSummary:
This is among the safest countries in the world for transgender visitors. Its legal framework for LGBTI rights is consistently assessed as the region's strongest (every year since 2015): gender identity and expression are protected from discrimination in law, legal gender recognition works by self-determination, and "X" gender markers are available on passports. Conversion therapy is banned and the constitution guarantees LGBTI equality.

The country records one of the lowest rates of physical or sexual victimisation of LGBTIQ+ people across a 27-country regional survey, and the national police force has adopted hate-crime procedures for SOGIE incidents. A foreign government's travel advisory describes it as a safe environment for foreign LGBT travellers, and no government travel advisory flags trans-specific concerns.

Residual risks are minor: non-physical harassment (including online) is more common than violence but tends to be under-reported, and — in the unlikely event of arrest — prison practice has been found to lag the country's progressive law, with transgender inmates reporting gaps in healthcare and placement procedures.
blindOutOfScope: Petty crime around nightclubs and tourist spots, and general counter-terrorism travel guidance, are ordinary travel risks that affect everyone.

Encyclopedia overview: this country is among the world's most progressive on LGBTI rights — same-sex activity legal since 1973, marriage equality, comprehensive discrimination protections, transgender rights, non-binary birth certificates, intersex rights, conversion-therapy ban, blood-donation equality.

National-university master's dissertation (2024): lived experiences of transgender inmates in this country's correctional agency — interviews with four current/former trans inmates; obstacles during and after incarceration relate to healthcare, legislation, knowledge/education gaps and post-release life.
